subject: RRBS: merging data from two runs of the same sample

messages.author: c02737bb0ac0a7f0
messages.subject: RRBS: merging data from two runs of the same sample
parts:
Hello,

I'm analyzing RRBS data sets that come from two different runs. I have my data in a processed form (containing coverage, freqC, freqT for each position).

Some of the samples were run in both runs, and I want to merge them into one data table, before feeding them into the routine methylkit analysis pipeline. So, I was wondering if there is an easy way to merge two (or more) runs of the same sample into one? Is there maybe some function in methylKit that can do that?

Thanks,
Alex

messages.author: c02737bb0ac0a7f0
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] RRBS: merging data from two runs of the same sample
parts:
Thanks,

I checked pool() function, it's very close to what I need.

The only problem for me is, pool() seems to work by merging all samples of the same group (with the same "treatment" setting) into one. (and I want to merge only the "technical" replicates, but leave the "biological" replicates intact).

I think I can try and load the groups of replicates that I want to merge as separate methylRawList objects, then for each of these, to apply the unite() function with the option min.per.group = 1L (since I don't want to lose any sites which only appear in one replicate), and then merge them with pool() into a new methylBase object with just one sample in it. However, then I will need a way of combining all these methylBase objects into one, and assign treatment settings for each of them.
Is it possible to do in methylKit? (combining methylBase objects into a bigger one with multiple samples in it).

BTW, on a more general note,
I wonder if the approach that I'm trying to pursue (merging the processed methylation data sets for replicate runs) is considered a valid one, or the recommended way of going about it is to start with raw sequencing data, concatenate them, and follow the entire Bismark pipeline from the scratch?

Thanks,
Alex

messages.author: e4181d5c40fc094c
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] RRBS: merging data from two runs of the same sample
parts:
At some point I faced a similar situation and tried a similar approach to what you have detailed. But later, the downstream processing was so much confusing that I had to start again by concatenating the reads into single file. Starting again proved straight forward and easy (no extra effort for the grey matter in my brain).

You may also start by concatenating the .sam output from the bismark alignment or a better option would be to concatenate the output from methylation extracter.

Regards,
Kalyan

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] RRBS: merging data from two runs of the same sample
parts:
I think you can create a "fake" treatment vector (same numbers for technical replicates) and new sample names with reorganize(), do pool(), following that use reorganize() again to set the real treatment vector. 
I think something like that should work

Best,
Altuna
